<section class="proj-q" aria-labelledby="h-question">
<h2 id="h-question"><i class="bi bi-question-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Research question</h2>
<p class="proj-question">Can uncertainty metrics of a wind power model&#x27;s inputs (weather data products, forecast ensembles and turbine-level data) predict calibrated plant-level power uncertainty at wind plants that have no power measurements?</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-contribution">
<h2 id="h-contribution"><i class="bi bi-person-check" aria-hidden="true"></i>My contribution</h2>
<p>Ph.D. researcher on The University of Texas at Dallas part of the project. I developed the surrogate-modeling workflow (calibrated uncertainty targets, surrogate models and validation on held-out plants) and implemented the project&#x27;s uncertainty metrics in Python, with funding from the U.S. Department of Energy through the National Renewable Energy Laboratory.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-method">
<h2 id="h-method"><i class="bi bi-diagram-3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Method</h2>
<p>Moving-window, data-source, ensemble-spread and spatial (variogram) uncertainty metrics as inputs; pinball-loss-optimal scales of a predictive distribution around the point forecast as targets at observed plants; Gaussian process regression and other regressors as surrogates; validation by holding out whole plants, scored with pinball loss, CRPS and reliability, with recalibration of the predictive distributions.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec proj-bounds" aria-labelledby="h-bounds">
<h2 id="h-bounds"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Boundary conditions</h2>
<p>No paper. The public framework is a fresh implementation tested on synthetic data; project data and results are not public.</p>
</section>
